title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: design custom AI agents with the AI development toolkit
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, sandbox-only preview scope, consumption billing and control paths are supported by the sources checked. Two governance checklist steps have no corresponding control-table row; these are minor consistency findings.

claims.claim: Business Central provides an in-product experience for designing custom AI agents as part of the AI development toolkit.
claims.quote: The ability to design agents is part of the AI development toolkit

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The designer is documented as a prerelease preview feature.
claims.quote: [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The in-product AI development toolkit is available only in sandbox environments, not production.
claims.quote: **Sandbox only**: Available exclusively in sandbox environments; never in production

claims.claim: The sandbox prerequisite starts at Business Central version 27.2.
claims.quote: A sandbox environment for testing and experimentation from version 27.2

claims.claim: Learn primarily addresses product owners, domain experts, consultants and developers experimenting with AI capabilities.
claims.quote: This article is primarily intended for product owners, domain experts, consultants, and developers who want to experiment with AI capabilities in Business Central.

claims.claim: The designer is intended for prototyping before building production solutions in AL extensions.
claims.quote: **Graduate** - Export learnings to build production solutions using AL extensions

claims.claim: Learn currently lists English as the only supported language.
claims.quote: This feature currently supports only English as language. While this feature can be used in other languages, it might not function as intended.

claims.claim: Users create and configure an agent through the Create agent wizard.
claims.quote: The **Create agent** wizard allows you to configure your agent by setting up its instructions, profile, and permissions.

claims.claim: Agent instructions are written in natural language.
claims.quote: Instructions are natural language descriptions that define your agent's purpose and behavior.

claims.claim: The wizard lets a user assign an agent profile.
claims.quote: Under **Profile (role)**, use the **Setup profile** option to select the profile that determines what UI elements the agent can see and interact with.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: An agent has assigned permission sets controlling its data and action access.
claims.quote: The agent is considered as a user in Business Central, so it can be assigned permission sets to control what data and actions it can access.

claims.claim: Creating tasks is a way to invoke an active agent.
claims.quote: Tasks are a way to trigger the agent. Tasks can only be added when the agent is active

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: Each newly created agent is Disabled by default and must be activated before use.
claims.quote: An agent is by default in the **Disabled** state. You must activate the agent to use it

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: An agent is represented as a user in Business Central.
claims.quote: The agent is considered as a user in Business Central

claims.claim: The roadmap describes custom agents as extending the runtime capabilities used by built-in Business Central agents.
claims.quote: extending the same agent runtime capabilities used by built-in Business Central agents.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes import and export of agent definitions as JSON files.
claims.quote: These definitions are stored as simple JSON files containing properties such as agent identity, instructions, assigned profiles, and permissions.

claims.claim: The Learn export page instead describes exported agent configurations as XML.
claims.quote: The exported agent appears in your **Downloads** window in .xml format.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap says custom agents have no built-in integrations for automatic email, event or recurring scheduled triggers yet.
claims.quote: there aren't yet any built-in integrations to automatically trigger these custom agents based on incoming emails, events, or scheduled recurrences

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap says professional developers can implement those triggers using AI Development Toolkit APIs.
claims.quote: this can be done by professional developers using the APIs available in the AI Development Toolkit

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The supplied roadmap record still has status In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is October CY2026, a target month already past on the November 2026 run date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is February CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "February CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).

claims.quote:

    "General Availability",

claims.claim: Copilot and agent capabilities are active by default when available in preview or generally available, so the capability itself needs no initial administrator activation.
claims.quote: Copilot and agent capabilities are active by default when they're available in preview or generally available.

claims.where: summary; Scope; Governance controls: design rights
claims.claim: AGENT - ADMIN grants permission to design agents.
claims.quote: "AGENT - ADMIN" gives you permission to design agents.

claims.claim: AGENT - DIAGNOSTICS additionally exposes execution cost and the serialised page in agent task log entries.
claims.quote: "AGENT - DIAGNOSTICS" gives you access to see the execution cost and the serialized page in the agent task log entries.

claims.claim: The Custom Agent capability must be enabled to use the designer.
claims.quote: Enable the **Custom Agent** capability in Business Central.

claims.where: Scope; Cost and licensing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Billing setup for agent capabilities in the tenant is a toolkit prerequisite.
claims.quote: Billing setup for agent capabilities in your tenant.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: An agent can read and change Business Central data within its effective permissions.
claims.quote: The agent can read and modify customers (both user and agent have these permissions)

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Tenant Copilot Credit capacity is shared with other Business Central environments and Microsoft services.
claims.quote: Copilot Credit capacity on the tenant is consumed by Business Central environments and other Microsoft services on the tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Toolkit sandboxes can contain customer data, including copies of production data.
claims.quote: **Sandbox data**: Can be used with customer data in sandbox environments (including sandbox copies of production data)

claims.claim: Learn says not to use the toolkit when compliance or security evaluation is the primary goal.
claims.quote:
Don't use the AI development toolkit when:

- **Compliance or security evaluation** is the primary goal

claims.claim: The overview says agents cannot have more permissions than their creating user.
claims.quote: **Permission inheritance**: Agents can't have more permissions than their creating user

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The permissions documentation says scheduled tasks run with the intersection of the scheduling user's and agent's permissions.
claims.quote: When a user schedules a task for an agent, the task is executed with permissions from the intersection of the user's permissions and the agent's permissions.

claims.claim: The transparency note instead describes intersection with the task approver's permissions.
claims.quote: It then runs with the intersection of the permissions given to the agent with the permissions of the user that approved the task

claims.claim: The transparency note uses the agent configurator's permissions when task approval was not required.
claims.quote: or the user that configured the agent, if task approval wasn't required.

claims.claim: Following a user intervention request, the task proceeds with the permissions of the responding user.
claims.quote: If the agent makes a user intervention request, the task continues proceeding with the *permissions of the user that responded to that intervention request*.

claims.claim: The responding user may differ from the task creator.
claims.quote: This user might be different from the task creator.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The assigned profile limits which UI elements an agent can see and interact with.
claims.quote: The agent is assigned to a profile (role) that determines which UI elements it can see and interact with.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The InsertAllowed page customisation property can disallow insertion by the agent.
claims.quote: | `InsertAllowed` | Boolean | `false`, the insert action isn't allowed for the agent. |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The DeleteAllowed page customisation property can disallow deletion by the agent.
claims.quote: | `DeleteAllowed` | Boolean | `false`, the delete action isn't allowed for the agent. |

claims.claim: Learn recommends creating custom profiles specifically for agents.
claims.quote: it's highly recommended to create custom profiles specifically for agents

claims.claim: Learn describes a move to GPT-5.3-chat as the default agent model.
claims.quote: **GPT-5.3-chat is now the default model for agents**

claims.claim: The agent model rollout is gradual.
claims.quote: This change rolls out gradually to environments across all regions.

claims.claim: The model update applies from version 28 onwards.
claims.quote: agents in Business Central are moving to GPT-5.3-chat as the default language model for version 28 and onwards.

claims.claim: UK, India and Australia environments are excluded from the initial model rollout.
claims.quote: Environments in the UK, India, and Australia are excluded from this initial rollout and will receive the update at a later date.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn recommends re-evaluating designed and coded agents after their model updates.
claims.quote: we highly recommend that you reevaluate your agents when the model has updated

claims.claim: Model updates can affect agent behaviour and accuracy.
claims.quote: because agent behavior, as well as accuracy, might be affected.

claims.claim: Preview features and behaviour can change without notice.
claims.quote: **Preview functionality**: Features and behavior might change without notice

claims.where: summary; front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The usage meter for billable Business Central agents is Copilot Credits, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: These capabilities use Copilot Credits for AI interactions and tasks, like retrieving information and responding to prompts. *Copilot Credits* are the billing units that measure usage.

claims.claim: Credit consumption depends on agent design, interaction frequency and the features used.
claims.quote: The number of Copilot Credits consumed by an agent depends on the design of the agent, how often customers interact with it, and the features they use.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The billing page says AI development toolkit billing events will be announced in a future update.
claims.quote:
### AI development toolkit (preview)

Billing events for the AI development toolkit will be announced in a future update.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Feature-specific Copilot Credit rates and billing quota are not published for the AI development toolkit at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central Custom Agent Allow data movement geography AI development toolkit pricing billing events credits; opened toolkit overview and consumption-billing page, whose toolkit section defers billing events and gives no toolkit rate or quota.

claims.claim: The billing page publishes separate rates for Sales Order Agent, Payables Agent and Expense Agent.
claims.quote:
### Expense Agent (preview) billing
...
### Sales Order Agent billing
...

claims.claim: The transparency note instead describes responsibility for Azure OpenAI operating costs attached to the customer's key.
claims.quote: Because your AI features are attached to your Azure OpenAI Service key, you're responsible for the operating costs of Azure OpenAI resources throughout development, testing and when your customers use the feature in production or sandbox environments.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Business Central supports prepaid capacity using Copilot Credit pack subscriptions.
claims.quote: The prepaid capacity model uses Copilot Credit pack subscriptions

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Business Central also supports pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Business Central supports two billing models: prepaid capacity and pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity is consumed first when both billing models are present.
claims.quote: Both billing models can be used in the Business Central environment. When available, prepaid capacity is consumed first.

claims.claim: Without additional setup, Business Central environments draw credit capacity from the tenant's default Power Platform environment.
claims.quote: Without any extra setup, Business Central environments automatically consume Copilot Credit capacity from the [default Power Platform environment]

claims.where: controls[2].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls

claims.quote: It isn't possible to allocate capacity to specific Microsoft services or features.

claims.claim: When quota is depleted, the AI capability is unavailable until capacity is added.
claims.quote: When the quota is depleted, the AI capability is unavailable until more capacity is added.

claims.claim: Learn does not publish a feature-specific price for the designer.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central Custom Agent Allow data movement geography AI development toolkit pricing billing events credits; opened toolkit overview and consumption-billing page. The latter defers toolkit billing events and links general Copilot pricing rather than a designer price.

claims.claim: The separate Agent SDK for AL is available in production from version 28.1.
claims.quote: The Agent SDK for AL is available in sandbox environments and, starting from version 28.1, also in production environments.

claims.claim: In Business Central, Copilot & agent capabilities > select the feature > Activate or Deactivate controls capability availability.
claims.quote:
To turn on a feature, select it in the list, and then select **Activate**.
    - To turn off a feature, select it in the list, and then select **Deactivate**.

claims.claim: No administrator automation for activating or deactivating the Custom Agent capability is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central administration API "Copilot" "capabilities" "data movement"; opened enable-ai, administration-center-api and the System.AI Copilot Capability reference. No capability activation setter was documented.

claims.claim: Configuring Copilot capabilities requires SUPER permission or one of the administrator licences listed by Learn.
claims.quote: You need **SUPER** permission in your Business Central user account or one of the following Business Central licenses:

claims.claim: The design capability is listed under Production ready previews.
claims.quote: The design capability is listed under **Production ready previews**.

claims.claim: Business Central > Copilot & agent capabilities > Allow data movement toggle configures cross-geography processing.
claims.quote:
enter **Copilot & agent capabilities**, and then choose the related link.
2. Switch the **Allow data movement** toggle on or off as desired.

claims.claim: No API equivalent of Business Central's Allow data movement toggle is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Central" "Allow data movement" "API" "admin"; opened enable-ai, ai-copilot-data-movement, administration-center-api and the Copilot Capability codeunit reference. No toggle-setting API was found.

claims.claim: The Allow data movement toggle appears only when capabilities might process data in another Azure geography.
claims.quote: The **Allow data movement** toggle appears when one or more copilot and agent capabilities might process data in a different Azure geography from the Business Central environment.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: data movement; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly identify whether the Allow data movement toggle affects Custom Agent.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Central" "Custom Agent" "data movement"; opened enable-ai, ai-copilot-data-movement and toolkit overview. General rules cover Microsoft-managed resources; no Custom Agent-specific applicability statement was found, and the transparency note describes an own-key model.

claims.claim: The capacity path is Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Prepaid capacity > Manage Capacity.
claims.quote:
under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**.
4. Select the **Summary** tab.
5. Complete one of the following actions:

    - Select **Manage Capacity** from the **Prepaid capacity** card.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 accepts an environment scope and allocatedEntitlements containing MCSMessages and allocation.quantity.
claims.quote:
scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId }
...
entitlementId    = "MCSMessages"
allocation       = @{ quantity = 5000 }
...
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: Allocated Power Platform environment capacity governs a Business Central environment once the two are linked.
claims.quote: Once completed, consumption of the Copilot Credits in the Business Central environment is limited by the capacity allocated to the linked Power Platform environment.

claims.claim: Only internal administrators can link the Business Central and Power Platform environments.
claims.quote: Link the Business Central environment to the Power Platform environment. Only internal admins can complete this task.

claims.claim: Allocation API use requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role allowed to manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the **Power Platform Administrator** or **Global Administrator** role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls: overages
claims.claim: Clearing both tenant-capacity draw and pay-as-you-go overages restricts consumption to allocated prepaid credits.
claims.quote: If no overage source is enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits.

claims.claim: Some capability changes apply immediately and others require users to sign out and back in.
claims.quote: Some AI features take effect immediately, while others require users to sign out and sign in again.

claims.where: Governance controls: Create agent wizard permissions
claims.claim: Agent > Create opens the wizard, whose Permissions section has Manage permissions.
claims.quote: Under **Permissions**, use **Manage permissions** to add the permissions that the agent should have.

claims.where: Governance controls: Create agent wizard profile
claims.claim: The Create agent wizard's Profile (role) section provides Setup profile.
claims.quote: Under **Profile (role)**, use the **Setup profile** option to select the profile

claims.claim: Learn documents Agent.UpdateAccessControl for assigning permission sets.
claims.quote: The `UpdateAccessControl` method replaces any existing permission sets with the ones you provide:

claims.claim: Learn documents Agent.SetProfile for assigning an agent profile.
claims.quote:
// Assign a profile
    Agent.SetProfile(AgentUserSecurityID, 'ACCOUNTANT', SystemApplicationAppId);

claims.claim: Toolkit configuration methods are restricted across application boundaries, rather than unrestricted administrator APIs for designer-created agents.
claims.quote: Creating instances, tasks, messages and any configuration changes targeting an agent defined in a different application is blocked with an error.

claims.claim: Business Central does not yet provide granular object-level permissions restricting Copilot configuration to particular administrators.
claims.quote: Business Central doesn't yet offer granular, object-level permissions so that only specific administrators can configure Copilot.

claims.claim: The linked Business Central permissions page explains how to assign permission sets to users.
claims.quote:
You can assign permissions sets to users in two ways:

- From the **User Card** page, by selecting permission sets to assign to the user.

claims.claim: The allocation API tutorial requires an app registration configured for Power Platform API.
claims.quote: An [app registration configured for Power Platform API](programmability-authentication-v2).

claims.claim: The TenantPool enforcement rule maps to Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: The **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant** option in the admin center maps to the `TenantPool` enforcement rule

claims.claim: Enabling TenantPool allows continued consumption from unallocated tenant capacity after the environment's allocation is exhausted.
claims.quote: when it's enabled, the environment continues to draw from unallocated tenant capacity after its own allocation is exhausted

claims.claim: The allocation tutorial describes disabling TenantPool as capping the environment at its allocation.
claims.quote: when it's disabled, the environment is capped at its allocation.

claims.claim: A published environment group rule governing tenant-capacity draw prevents overriding that setting for an individual environment.
claims.quote: If a published [environment group rule](environment-groups#rules) governs **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant**, you can't override the setting for an individual environment.

claims.claim: Attempts to update that group-controlled setting are rejected with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.

claims.claim: Agent configuration export can be used to back up definitions.
claims.quote: The purpose of this feature is to allow you to back up your agent configuration, share it with others, or move it between different sandbox environments.

claims.claim: The roadmap recommends storing exported definitions in source control such as GitHub.
claims.quote: We recommend storing these files in a source control system like GitHub to track changes and maintain version history.

claims.quote: Grant agents only the permission sets their task needs, remembering that each task runs with the intersection of the user's and the agent's permissions. | The table covers capability activation, data movement and credit capacity, not agent permission sets.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist item beginning 'Grant agents only the permission sets'. Keep the verified permissions discussion and wizard path elsewhere; do not add a control row.
